sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Observability interview questions cover the three pillars (metrics, logs, traces) plus the engineering culture around them — Micrometer + Prometheus + Grafana, structured logging (JSON, MDC, correlation IDs), distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry, Zipkin, Jaeger), SLI/SLO/SLA definitions, error budgets, the four golden signals, alerting design (avoiding alert fatigue), and the pragmatic question every senior interview asks: "what would you instrument first in a brand-new service?". For incident response and on-call see the SRE page.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Three pillars + one outcome:

- **Metrics** — counter, gauge, histogram (Micrometer + Prometheus).
- **Logs** — structured JSON + correlation ID; ship to ELK / Loki / Splunk.
- **Traces** — OpenTelemetry, Jaeger / Zipkin / Tempo.
- **Outcome** = SLI / SLO / error budget — *that's the language ops talks*.

**Four golden signals**: latency, traffic, errors, saturation.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Cardinality** kills metrics — never put `userId` in a label.
- **MDC** propagates correlation IDs through `Logger`; lose it on async hops.
- **Sampling** is a trade-off — head-based easy, tail-based smarter.
- **Alert fatigue** — page on SLO burn-rate, not raw thresholds.
- **Health checks** ≠ readiness — liveness restarts, readiness gates traffic.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd instrument the four golden signals with Micrometer → Prometheus, structured logs with correlation IDs in MDC, distributed tracing via OpenTelemetry, and define SLOs that drive burn-rate alerts — paging humans only on user-visible regressions."*
